docs.text: الطريقة متى تُستخدم الخطوات Import YAML دون Helm إطلاقاً شغّل helm template ea-hub deploy/helm/ea-hub -n ea-hub -f my-values.yaml > ea-hub.yaml على أي جهاز، ثم اختر في العنقود ⬆ Import YAML، والصق الناتج، واختر مساحة الأسماء ea-hub. أو استخدم deploy/kubernetes/ea-hub.yaml مع الـ Secret الخاص بك، كما في kubernetes.md Continuous Delivery (Fleet أو GitOps) عدة عناقيد، والتغييرات تمر عبر Git أضف GitRepo يشير إلى هذا المستودع بالمسار deploy/helm/ea-hub. احفظ إعداداتك في Kubernetes Secret، وأشر إليه بـ helm.valuesFrom داخل ملف fleet.yaml في مستودع الإعدادات الخاص بك

docs.title: 8. DNS وHTTPS
docs.text:
1. اعرف عنوان الـ ingress: من Explore ← Service Discovery ← Ingresses ← ea-hub، أو بالأمر kubectl -n ea-hub get ingress.
  2. أنشئ سجل DNS: سجل من نوع A للاسم hub.example.com يشير إلى ذلك العنوان، أو إلى عنوان موزّع الحمل.
  3. الشهادة: مع cert-manager وClusterIssuer باسم letsencrypt تُصدر الشهادة تلقائياً. دون cert-manager، أنشئ TLS secret باسم ea-hub-tls من Explore ← Storage ← Secrets ← TLS Certificate.

docs.title: 9. افتح الموقع وسجّل الدخول
docs.text: افتح https://hub.example.com/admin:

docs.title: 10. التشغيل اليومي من Rancher
docs.text: المهمة من واجهة Rancher بالأوامر السجلات Workloads ← ea-hub ← ⋮ ← View Logs (اختر الحاوية migrate أو app) kubectl -n ea-hub logs deploy/ea-hub -f نسخة احتياطية الآن Workloads ← CronJobs ← ea-hub-backup ← ⋮ ← Run Now kubectl -n ea-hub create job --from=cronjob/ea-hub-backup backup-now الترقية Apps ← Installed Apps ← ea-hub ← Upgrade (إن ثبّتّه من الكتالوج) helm upgrade ea-hub deploy/helm/ea-hub -n ea-hub -f my-values.yaml --set image.tag=<new> المراقبة ثبّت تطبيق Monitoring، فيظهر استهلاك المعالج والذاكرة تحت Workloads لقطات الأقراص واجهة Longhorn ← Volumes ← ea-hub-* ← جدول اللقطات أو النسخ إزالة التثبيت مع الإبقاء على البيانات Apps ← Installed Apps ← ⋮ ← Delete helm uninstall ea-hub -n ea-hub

docs.title: حل المشكلات
docs.text:
العَرَض الحل الـ Ingress يعيد 404 قيمة ingress.className خاطئة: استخدم nginx في RKE2 وtraefik في K3s. تحقق بالأمر kubectl get ingressclass القرص (PVC) في حالة Pending لا يوجد StorageClass افتراضي. عيّنه في Rancher (Storage ← StorageClasses ← ⋮ ← Set as Default)، أو مرّر قيم storageClass Pod Security Admission يمنع الحاويات يعمل الـ chart دون صلاحيات root، مع seccomp RuntimeDefault، ويُسقط كل الصلاحيات، فيتوافق مع سياسة restricted. راجع أي قاعدة مخصصة في PSA أو Kyverno أو Gatekeeper ImagePullBackOff يجب أن يكون الـ pull secret في مساحة الأسماء ea-hub، ومذكوراً في imagePullSecrets

باقي الخطوات مطابقة للدليل العام: kubernetes.md وhelm.md.

docs.title: الدخول الموحد (OpenID Connect)
docs.text:
يمكن تسجيل الدخول إلى EA-Hub بحساب المؤسسة عبر أي مزوّد OpenID Connect، مثل Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) وKeycloak وOkta وAuth0 وGoogle Workspace وAuthentik وPing. يبقى الدخول بكلمة المرور متاحاً بجانبه.

عند تفعيل الدخول الموحد، يظهر في صفحة دخول المدير زر Sign in with your organisation account.

النسخة الإنجليزية: en/single-sign-on.md

docs.title: كيف يُقرَّر من يدخل
docs.text:
الشخص ما يحدث عند الدخول نطاق بريده ليس في OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS (عند ضبط هذه القائمة) يُرفض بريده الموثَّق مذكور في OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS، أو هو عضو في مجموعة مذكورة في OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS يدخل، ويُنشأ حسابه إن لم يكن موجوداً، ويحصل على دور المدير لديه حساب في EA-Hub بالبريد الموثَّق نفسه يدخل إلى ذلك الحساب، وتبقى أدواره كما هي أي شخص آخر يُرفض، إلا إن ضُبط OIDC_AUTO_CREATE=true مع OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS، فيُنشأ له حساب بلا أدوار

قواعد أخرى:

  • البريد الموثَّق فقط: لا يستخدم EA-Hub عنوان البريد لإيجاد حساب أو إنشائه إلا إن أكّده المزوّد. يقبل أحد أمرين:
  • القيمة email_verified مساوية لـ true.
  • القيمة xms_edov في Microsoft Entra ID مساوية لـ true، أي أن نطاق البريد موثَّق في مستأجرك (tenant).
  • البريد غير الموثَّق: إن لم يرسل مزوّدك أياً منهما، يمكنك ضبط OIDC_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL=false، لكن مع OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS فقط. عندها:
  • لا يُربط البريد غير الموثَّق بأي حساب موجود.
  • لا يطابق OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS، فلا يمنح دور المدير إلا OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS.
  • حدّد النطاقات: اضبط دائماً OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS على نطاقات مؤسستك. هذا مهم خاصة مع المزوّدين المشتركين مثل Google (https://accounts.google.com)، الذي يسمح بدخول أي حساب Google.
  • صلاحيات المدير تُضاف ولا تُسحب تلقائياً: لسحبها، احذف الدور من داخل EA-Hub.
  • إيقاف موظف: إيقاف الشخص عند المزوّد يمنع الدخول الجديد فوراً، لكن جلسته المفتوحة في EA-Hub تبقى حتى ينتهي رمز التحديث، أي حتى 30 يوماً. لإنهائها فوراً، أوقف المستخدم أو احذف حسابه من EA-Hub.
  • فحوص الأمان:
  • يتم الدخول بتدفق authorization code مع PKCE وstate وnonce.
  • يُتحقق من توقيع رمز الهوية بمفاتيح المزوّد المنشورة، ومن المُصدِر والجمهور وتاريخ الانتهاء.
  • عنوان الرجوع ثابت على APP_URL.

docs.title: 1. سجّل EA-Hub عند المزوّد
docs.text:
يحتاج كل مزوّد إلى ثلاثة أمور:

  • نوع التطبيق: تطبيق ويب (confidential client) بتدفق authorization code.
  • عنوان الرجوع (Redirect URI): https://<عنوان EA-Hub>/api/selfhost/auth/oidc/callback، مثل https://hub.example.com/api/selfhost/auth/oidc/callback.
  • النطاقات (Scopes): openid email profile، مع إضافة بيانات المجموعات إن كنت ستستخدم OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS.

احتفظ بـ رابط المُصدِر (issuer) ومعرّف العميل (client ID) وسر العميل (client secret).

المزوّد رابط المُصدِر ملاحظات Microsoft Entra ID https://login.microsoftonline.com/<tenant-id>/v2.0 App registrations ← New registration بمنصة Web، ثم أضف client secret. من Token configuration ← Add optional claim ← ID أضف email وxms_edov. للمجموعات استخدم Add groups claim. يرسل Entra معرّفات المجموعات (object IDs)، فضعها في OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS Keycloak https://<keycloak>/realms/<realm> أنشئ client مع تفعيل Client authentication وStandard flow. للمجموعات أضف mapper من نوع Group Membership باسم groups، مع إلغاء Full group path Okta https://<your-org>.okta.com (أو رابط خادم تفويض مخصص) أنشئ OIDC – Web Application. للمجموعات أضف قيمة groups إلى ID token Google Workspace https://accounts.google.com أنشئ OAuth client ID من نوع Web application. لا ترسل Google المجموعات، فاستخدم OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS Authentik https://<authentik>/application/o/<app-slug> أنشئ OAuth2/OpenID Provider بنوع عميل Confidential

docs.title: 2. اضبط EA-Hub
docs.text:
Docker Compose: أضف ما يلي إلى .env، ثم شغّل docker compose up -d:

OIDC_ISSUER=https://login.microsoftonline.com/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000/v2.0
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=<client secret>
OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=yourcompany.com
OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS=you@yourcompany.com
OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS=                     # optional

Helm:

sso:
  oidc:
    issuer: https://kc.example.com/realms/acme
    clientId: ea-hub
    clientSecret: "<client secret>"     # or key oidc-client-secret in secrets.existingSecret
    allowedDomains: acme.com
    adminGroups: ea-admins
    # adminEmails: you@acme.com

منصات Container-as-a-Service: اضبط متغيرات OIDC_* نفسها، واحفظ OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET في مخزن الأسرار الخاص بالمنصة.

docs.title: 3. جرّبه
docs.text: افتح https://<عنوانك>/admin، واضغط Sign in with your organisation account. بعد صفحة دخول المزوّد تعود إلى لوحة التحكم.

docs.title: كل الإعدادات
docs.text: المتغير قيمة Helm الافتراضي المعنى OIDC_ISSUER sso.oidc.issuer – رابط مُصدِر المزوّد. يقرأ EA-Hub منه <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration OIDC_CLIENT_ID sso.oidc.clientId – معرّف العميل OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET sso.oidc.clientSecret – سر العميل، ويُرسل بمصادقة HTTP Basic إلى نقطة الرموز OIDC_SCOPES sso.oidc.scopes openid email profile النطاقات المطلوبة OIDC_BUTTON_LABEL sso.oidc.buttonLabel Sign in with your organisation account نص الزر OIDC_ADMIN_EMAILS sso.oidc.adminEmails – عناوين بريد يحصل أصحابها على دور المدير، مفصولة بفواصل OIDC_ADMIN_GROUPS sso.oidc.adminGroups – مجموعات يحصل أعضاؤها على دور المدير، مفصولة بفواصل OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM sso.oidc.groupsClaim groups اسم الحقل في ID token الذي يحتوي على المجموعات OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS sso.oidc.allowedDomains – نطاقات البريد المسموح لها بالدخول، مفصولة بفواصل (موصى به) OIDC_AUTO_CREATE sso.oidc.autoCreate false إنشاء حساب بلا أدوار لأي شخص من OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS OIDC_REQUIRE_VERIFIED_EMAIL sso.oidc.requireVerifiedEmail true اشتراط أن تكون email_verified (أو xms_edov في Entra) مساوية لـ true

docs.title: حل المشكلات
docs.text: الرسالة في صفحة الدخول السبب ليس لحساب مؤسستك صلاحية دخول EA-Hub بعد الشخص ليس لديه حساب في EA-Hub وليس مذكوراً كمدير، أو نطاق بريده ليس في OIDC_ALLOWED_DOMAINS. أنشئ له حساباً في EA-Hub، أو أضفه إلى القائمة لم تؤكد مؤسستك عنوان بريدك رمز الهوية لا يحتوي على email_verified=true ولا xms_edov=true. في Entra ID أضف الحقل الاختياري xms_edov لم يكتمل الدخول الموحد ابحث في سجلات التطبيق عن [selfhost] SSO sign-in failed:. الأسباب الشائعة: عنوان رجوع لا يطابق APP_URL، أو سر عميل خاطئ، أو فرق في الساعة أكثر من دقيقتين الدخول الموحد غير متاح حالياً لم يستطع EA-Hub الوصول إلى <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration. تحقق من رابط المُصدِر ومن اتصال الخادم بالإنترنت

docs.title: حل المشكلات الشائعة
docs.text:
ابدأ دائماً بهذين الأمرين:

docker compose ps                  # أي خدمة متوقفة أو غير "healthy"؟
docker compose logs --tail=100 app migrate caddy

في Kubernetes استبدلهما بالأوامر التالية:

kubectl -n ea-hub get pods
kubectl -n ea-hub logs deploy/ea-hub -c migrate
kubectl -n ea-hub logs deploy/ea-hub

docs.title: APP_URL is missing — run ./setup.sh
docs.text: لا يوجد ملف .env، أو ينقصه متغير. شغّل ./setup.sh، أو انسخ .env.example إلى .env واملأه.

docs.title: خدمة migrate توقفت، والتطبيق لا يبدأ
docs.text:
اقرأ سجلها: docker compose logs migrate.

الرسالة الحل password authentication failed غُيّرت POSTGRES_PASSWORD بعد أول تشغيل. أعدها إلى قيمتها الأصلية. القاعدة تحفظ كلمة المرور الأولى ADMIN_PASSWORD must be at least 10 characters كلمة مرور المدير قصيرة. صحّحها في .env ثم نفّذ docker compose up -d waiting for database ثم توقف القاعدة لم تبدأ. انظر docker compose logs db، وغالباً السبب امتلاء القرص

ملاحظة: حالة migrate تكون exited (0) بعد النجاح، وهذا طبيعي.

docs.title: الموقع لا يفتح من المتصفح
docs.text:
• تأكد أن الخدمات تعمل: docker compose ps.
  • على الخادم نفسه جرّب curl http://localhost/healthz (أو مع المنفذ الذي اخترته). إن نجح هذا ولم يفتح الموقع من جهاز آخر، فافتح المنفذ في جدار الحماية: sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp.
  • إذا كان المنفذ 80 مستخدماً من برنامج آخر (IIS أو Apache)، فشغّل ./setup.sh واختر منفذاً آخر مثل 8080.

docs.title: شهادة HTTPS لا تصدر
docs.text:
• يجب أن يشير سجل DNS من نوع A إلى IP الخادم. تحقق بالأمر nslookup hub.example.com.
  • يجب أن يصل المنفذان 80 و443 إلى الخادم من الإنترنت.
  • اقرأ السجل: docker compose logs caddy.
  • داخل شبكة مغلقة بلا إنترنت لا يمكن الحصول على شهادة عامة. استخدم tls internal كما في install-docker.md.

docs.title: "بيانات الدخول غير صحيحة" مع كلمة مرور صحيحة
docs.text:
• البريد يجب أن يطابق ADMIN_EMAIL.
  • بعد 10 محاولات فاشلة خلال 15 دقيقة يُمنع الدخول مؤقتاً، فانتظر ربع ساعة.
  • إعادة تعيين كلمة مرور المدير: ضع كلمة جديدة في ADMIN_PASSWORD، واضبط ADMIN_RESET_PASSWORD=true في .env، ثم نفّذ: 
    docker compose up -d --force-recreate migrate app
    بعد الدخول أعد القيمة إلى ADMIN_RESET_PASSWORD=false.

docs.title: "نسيت كلمة المرور" لا يرسل بريداً
docs.text: لم يُضبط SMTP. أضف SMTP_HOST وSMTP_USER وSMTP_PASSWORD وSMTP_FROM إلى .env ثم نفّذ docker compose up -d. للمدير استخدم طريقة إعادة التعيين السابقة.

docs.title: الروابط في الرسائل أو الصور تشير إلى عنوان خاطئ
docs.text: APP_URL يجب أن يطابق العنوان الذي يفتحه الناس تماماً، بما في ذلك https والمنفذ إن وُجد. صحّحه ثم نفّذ docker compose up -d.

docs.title: الصور المرفوعة لا تظهر بعد تغيير العنوان
docs.text: الروابط الموقّعة مرتبطة بـ APP_URL. بعد تصحيحه أعد تحميل الصفحة، فالروابط تتجدد تلقائياً.

docs.title: رفع ملف كبير يفشل
docs.text: الحد الافتراضي 10 ميجابايت. غيّره عبر STORAGE_MAX_UPLOAD_MB في .env.

docs.title: البحث الدلالي أو المساعد أو Turnstile لا يعمل
docs.text: هذه ميزات اختيارية، وتعمل فقط حين تضع مفاتيحها في .env (انظر install-docker.md) ثم تعيد التشغيل.

docs.title: القرص امتلأ
docs.text:
• راجع حجم النسخ الاحتياطية: du -sh backups/*. قلّل BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS أو انقل النسخ القديمة.
  • نظّف صور Docker القديمة: docker image prune -f.

docs.title: تنزيل الصورة ghcr.io/... يفشل بالخطأ denied أو unauthorized
docs.text:
المستودع خاص. لديك حلان: - سجّل الدخول: docker login ghcr.io، واستخدم token فيه صلاحية read:packages. - أو ابنِ الصورة محلياً: docker compose build && docker compose up -d.

لا تزال المشكلة قائمة؟ افتح Issue في المستودع، وأرفق ناتج docker compose ps وdocker compose logs --tail=200 app migrate. احذف أي كلمة مرور قبل النشر.

docs.title: لا يوجد shell داخل حاوية التطبيق
docs.text:
منذ الإصدار 1.2 تُبنى صورة التطبيق على صورة distroless، وهي لا تحتوي shell ولا npm، وهذا يقلل الثغرات كثيراً. لذلك لا يعمل الأمر docker compose exec app sh. بدله شغّل Node مباشرة:

docker compose exec app node -e "console.log(process.version)"
docker compose run --rm migrate node selfhost/scripts/migrate.mjs

أما أوامر النسخ الاحتياطي وأوامر psql فتُشغَّل في حاويتي backup وdb، وفيهما shell كالمعتاد.

docs.title: Docker Compose
docs.text:
cd ea-hub-selfhost
git pull                      # آخر ملفات الإعداد والتوثيق
docker compose pull           # آخر صورة للتطبيق
docker compose up -d          # إعادة التشغيل بالنسخة الجديدة

إذا كنت تبني الصورة بنفسك، فاستبدل docker compose pull بالأمر docker compose build.

تُطبَّق تحديثات قاعدة البيانات تلقائياً عبر خدمة migrate قبل أن يبدأ التطبيق. بياناتك وملفاتك تبقى كما هي.

نصيحة: خذ نسخة احتياطية قبل كل تحديث كبير: 

docker compose exec backup sh /backup/backup.sh now

docs.title: تثبيت نسخة محددة بدلاً من الأحدث دائماً
docs.text: في .env استبدل latest برقم الإصدار، مثل EA_HUB_IMAGE=ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:1.2.0، ثم نفّذ docker compose up -d.

docs.title: Helm
docs.text:
git pull
helm upgrade ea-hub ./deploy/helm/ea-hub -n ea-hub --reset-then-reuse-values

استخدم --reset-then-reuse-values (Helm 3.14 أو أحدث) بدل --reuse-values: الأول يحتفظ بإعداداتك ويضيف إليها القيم الافتراضية للإعدادات الجديدة في الإصدار الجديد.

docs.title: نسخة احتياطية تلقائية قبل كل ترقية
docs.text:
قبل تطبيق تحديثات قاعدة البيانات تؤخذ نسخة احتياطية تلقائياً، فإن فشلت الترقية تعود إلى ما كنت عليه:

  • Docker Compose: في كل docker compose up تحفظ الخدمة backup-before-migrate نسخة في ./backups قبل خدمة migrate. لإيقافها اضبط BACKUP_BEFORE_MIGRATE=0 في .env.
  • Helm: في كل helm upgrade تأخذ مهمة ea-hub-backup-before-upgrade نسخة قبل الترقية. لإيقافها اضبط backup.beforeUpgrade=false.

docs.title: ترقية PostgreSQL إلى إصدار رئيسي جديد
docs.text:
• Docker Compose: شغّل selfhost/scripts/pg-major-upgrade.sh 17. يأخذ السكربت نسخة احتياطية، ويحتفظ بقرص البيانات القديم كما هو، ويشغّل الإصدار الجديد على قرص فارغ، ثم يستعيد البيانات، ويطبع أوامر التراجع. يُختبر الانتقال من 16 إلى 17 في CI.
  • Helm مع القاعدة المدمجة: خذ نسخة احتياطية، ثم ثبّت الإصدار الجديد على قرص جديد، واستعد البيانات بـ backup.sh restore. لا تغيّر الإصدار الرئيسي على قرص بيانات موجود.
  • CloudNativePG: اتبع طريقة المشغّل (operator) للترقية الرئيسية، وهي استيراد البيانات إلى Cluster جديد.

للتراجع عن ترقية فاشلة: 1. أعد الصورة إلى وسمها السابق (EA_HUB_IMAGE في .env، أو helm rollback ea-hub). 2. استعد آخر نسخة كما في backup.md: backup.sh list ثم backup.sh restore <اسم-النسخة>.

docs.title: لمشرفي هذا المستودع: متابعة المشروع الأصلي
docs.text:
المستودع الأصلي E20E-Tools/ea-hub-v2 هو المصدر (upstream). سير العمل upstream-sync.yml يعمل يومياً كالتالي:

  1. يجلب upstream/main.
  2. يدمجه في الفرع upstream-sync.
  3. يفتح طلب دمج (PR) إلى main، أو يحدّث الطلب المفتوح.

لا يُدمج أي شيء تلقائياً. راجع الطلب، وانتظر نجاح CI (الاختبارات وCompose وkind)، ثم ادمجه.

لنشر صورة جديدة على GHCR أنشئ وسماً (tag) برقم الإصدار، مثل git tag v1.0.0 && git push origin v1.0.0. النشر يكون مع الوسوم فقط، توفيراً لحصة التخزين المجانية.

docs.title: إعداد مرة واحدة: صلاحية قراءة المستودع الأصلي
docs.text:
المستودع الأصلي خاص، ولهذا يحتاج سير العمل token:

  1. في GitHub افتح: Settings ← Developer settings ← Fine-grained tokens ← Generate new token.
  2. اختر المالك E20E-Tools، ثم المستودعين ea-hub-v2 وea-hub-selfhost.
  3. الصلاحيات:
  4. على ea-hub-v2: Contents: Read.
  5. على ea-hub-selfhost: Contents: Read and write وPull requests: Read and write وWorkflows: Read and write.
  6. في ea-hub-selfhost افتح Settings ← Secrets and variables ← Actions ← New repository secret، وسمِّ السر UPSTREAM_TOKEN والصق الـ token.
  7. جرّب يدوياً: Actions ← Upstream sync ← Run workflow.

docs.title: إذا ظهر تعارض (conflict)
docs.text:
الملفات الخاصة بهذه النسخة، مثل README.md و.env.example وDockerfile وdocker-compose.yml، تُحفظ تلقائياً بنسختنا عبر .gitattributes. إذا تعارض ملف آخر، يفتح سير العمل طلباً مسودّة (draft) عنوانه DO NOT MERGE من الفرع upstream-sync-conflicts. لا تدمج هذا الطلب أبداً، فدمجه يحذف طبقة الاستضافة الذاتية. بدلاً من ذلك، حُلّ التعارض يدوياً ثم أغلق المسودّة:

git fetch origin
git checkout -B upstream-sync origin/main
git config merge.ours.driver true
git remote add upstream https://github.com/E20E-Tools/ea-hub-v2.git   # مرة واحدة
git fetch upstream main
git merge upstream/main          # حُلّ التعارضات ثم:
git commit
git push --force origin upstream-sync
gh pr create --head upstream-sync --base main --title "Sync with upstream"   # أو من واجهة GitHub

أكثر ما قد يتعارض هو src/server.ts وvite.config.ts وpackage.json، وفيها سطور قليلة مضافة لهذه النسخة ومعلّمة بكلمة Self-host. أبقِ تلك السطور، وخذ الباقي من الأصل.

docs.title: متى يجب تعديل طبقة الاستبدال؟
docs.text: إذا أضاف الأصل استخداماً جديداً لـ Supabase غير مدعوم في src/selfhost، مثل دالة جديدة في supabase-js، فستفشل الاختبارات في CI برسالة واضحة. عندها أضف الدعم في src/selfhost/supabase-js أو src/selfhost/server. التفاصيل في architecture.md.

docs.title: EA-Hub self-hosted — deployment guides (English)
docs.text:
EA-Hub runs anywhere that can run a Linux container and a PostgreSQL 16 database. Pick the guide that matches where you want to run it. Each guide is self-contained, from requirements to a signed-in admin.

All guides in one document: PDF · Word

Where you want to run it Best for Guide Docker on one machine (laptop, office server, cloud VM) Trying it out, small teams, simplest operations deploy-docker.md Local Kubernetes (Docker Desktop, kind, minikube, k3s) Learning, testing the Helm chart on your own computer deploy-kubernetes-local.md Any Kubernetes cluster (Helm chart or plain YAML) On-premises clusters, AKS / EKS / GKE / DOKS… deploy-kubernetes.md Red Hat OpenShift / OKD Enterprises standardised on OpenShift deploy-openshift.md Rancher (RKE2 / k3s clusters managed by Rancher) Teams that manage clusters through Rancher deploy-rancher.md Azure Container Apps Serverless containers on Azure deploy-azure-container-apps.md AWS ECS on Fargate Serverless containers on AWS deploy-aws-ecs-fargate.md Google Cloud Run Serverless containers on Google Cloud deploy-google-cloud-run.md

One-click cloud templates (Azure Bicep with a "Deploy to Azure" button, AWS CloudFormation, Google Cloud Terraform): deploy/cloud.

Several environments with GitOps (Argo CD, Rancher Fleet; staging and production values): deploy/gitops.

Server status: the admin console's Settings → Application health page shows the version, database, migrations, storage, e-mail, SSO, jobs, metrics and search status.

No internet access? Every release includes offline bundles (ea-hub-airgap-<version>-<arch>.tar.gz) with all images, the chart and the Compose files: selfhost/airgap.

Verify a release: - The image is signed with cosign. - It has SLSA build provenance: gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version> --repo E20E-Tools/ea-hub-selfhost. - An SPDX SBOM is attached to every GitHub Release.

Single sign-on (Microsoft Entra ID, Keycloak, Okta, Google…) works on every platform: see single-sign-on.md.

docs.title: What every installation is made of
docs.text: Part Docker / Kubernetes / OpenShift / Rancher Container-as-a-Service (Azure, AWS, Google) Web app container ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost same container Database PostgreSQL 16 container with a volume the provider's managed PostgreSQL 16 Database setup migrate service / init container MIGRATE_ON_START=true on the app Uploaded files a volume / PVC at /data/storage a network file share mounted at /data/storage HTTPS Caddy (Docker), Ingress or Route built into the platform Daily jobs cron service / CronJobs the platform's scheduled jobs Backups backup service / CronJob managed database backups + file-share snapshots

docs.title: Requirements common to all guides
docs.text:
• A container image. Released versions are published at ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version>. You can also build it yourself from this repository with docker build -t <your-registry>/ea-hub-selfhost:<tag> ..
  • PostgreSQL 16 or newer. The built-in one, or a managed service.
  • Persistent storage for uploaded files (5 GB is plenty to start with).
  • An address people will use, e.g. https://hub.example.com. The app must be told this exact address (APP_URL / appUrl).
  • The first admin's e-mail address and a password of at least 10 characters.
  • Optional: an SMTP account (password reset, notifications), an OpenAI key (search by meaning), Cloudflare Turnstile keys (bot protection). Each feature switches itself on only when its key is set.

Minimum resources for the whole system: 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, 20–35 GB disk. The details are in each guide.

docs.title: Settings reference
docs.text:
All guides use the same settings, under two names: environment variables (Docker and cloud) or Helm values.

Environment variable Helm value Meaning APP_URL appUrl Public address of the site (no trailing slash) APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY secrets.appEncryptionKey Root secret, 32+ random characters. Never change it after the first start CRON_SECRET secrets.cronSecret Secret the scheduled jobs send to the app DATABASE_URL or DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_NAME, APP_DB_USER, APP_DB_PASSWORD handled by the chart How the app connects to PostgreSQL DB_SSLMODE externalDatabase.sslmode require for most managed databases POSTGRES_PASSWORD / DATABASE_ADMIN_URL secrets.postgresPassword Admin connection used only to prepare the database MIGRATE_ON_START – true: prepare the database when the app starts (cloud platforms) ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD admin.email, admin.password First admin, created once STORAGE_DIR – Where uploads are stored (default /data/storage) TRUST_PROXY_HOPS trustProxyHops Proxies in front of the app that append to X-Forwarded-For (default 1) SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT, SMTP_SECURE, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASSWORD, SMTP_FROM smtp.* Outgoing e-mail OPENAI_API_KEY, TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY, GROQ_API_KEY features.* Optional features OIDC_* sso.oidc.* Single sign-on, see single-sign-on.md STORAGE_BACKEND, S3_* storage.backend, storage.s3.* Uploads on a volume (default) or in an S3-compatible bucket METRICS_TOKEN metrics.enabled Prometheus metrics at /metrics

Health check for any platform: GET /healthz returns {"ok":true,"database":"ok"}.

docs.title: Deploying EA-Hub on AWS (ECS on Fargate)
docs.text:
Amazon ECS with the Fargate launch type runs the EA-Hub container without servers to manage. The full setup on AWS:

EA-Hub part AWS service Web app ECS service on Fargate HTTPS entry point Application Load Balancer + ACM certificate Database Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 16 Uploaded files (/data/storage) Amazon EFS with an access point Secrets AWS Secrets Manager Daily jobs EventBridge Scheduler running ECS tasks Backups RDS automated backups + AWS Backup for EFS

Status: these steps follow AWS's documented CLI and console flows. The container itself, owner mode for managed PostgreSQL, and MIGRATE_ON_START are tested in CI on plain PostgreSQL 16. AWS itself has not been tested end-to-end yet.

Want Kubernetes on AWS instead? Use EKS with the Helm chart: deploy-kubernetes.md (StorageClass gp3, AWS Load Balancer Controller or ingress-nginx).

Faster: a ready-made template creates all of this in one step. See deploy/cloud. This guide explains each piece, if you prefer to build it by hand or adapt it.

docs.title: AWS resources and sizing
docs.text:
Resource Starting size Fargate task (app) 1 vCPU, 2 GB, 1–3 tasks Fargate task (each daily job) 0.25 vCPU, 0.5 GB, a few seconds per day RDS PostgreSQL db.t4g.small, 20 GB gp3, engine 16.x, single-AZ (Multi-AZ for production) EFS General Purpose, Bursting; pay per GB stored Application Load Balancer 1, internet-facing, in 2 public subnets

Rough cost at these sizes: about USD 60–90 per month in most regions.

docs.title: Tools, permissions and network
docs.text: Need Detail AWS account IAM permissions for ECS, EC2 (VPC, security groups), RDS, EFS, ELB, ACM, Secrets Manager, IAM roles, EventBridge Scheduler, CloudWatch Logs AWS CLI v2 configured with aws configure / SSO VPC 2 public subnets (load balancer) and 2 private subnets with a NAT gateway (tasks, database, EFS). The default VPC also works for a test, with public IPs on the tasks Image ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version> with a GitHub token (read:packages) stored in Secrets Manager, or a copy in Amazon ECR (recommended) Domain + ACM certificate for HTTPS: a domain in Route 53 or any DNS provider, and a certificate in ACM for hub.example.com

docs.title: 2. Variables
docs.text:
REGION=eu-central-1
VPC=vpc-xxxxxxxx
PRIV_SUBNETS=subnet-aaa,subnet-bbb        # tasks, RDS, EFS
PUB_SUBNETS=subnet-ccc,subnet-ddd         # load balancer
DOMAIN=hub.example.com
ACCOUNT=$(aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text)

docs.title: 3. Copy the image to ECR (recommended)
docs.text:
aws ecr create-repository --repository-name ea-hub-selfhost --region $REGION
aws ecr get-login-password --region $REGION | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin $ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.$REGION.amazonaws.com
docker pull ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version>     # or build it: docker build -t ea-hub-selfhost .
docker tag ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version> $ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.$REGION.amazonaws.com/ea-hub-selfhost:<version>
docker push $ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.$REGION.amazonaws.com/ea-hub-selfhost:<version>
IMAGE=$ACCOUNT.dkr.ecr.$REGION.amazonaws.com/ea-hub-selfhost:<version>

docs.title: 4. Security groups
docs.text:
Create three security groups in the VPC:

Group Inbound rule ea-hub-alb 443 and 80 from 0.0.0.0/0 ea-hub-app 3000 from ea-hub-alb ea-hub-data 5432 (PostgreSQL) and 2049 (NFS/EFS) from ea-hub-app

docs.title: 5. Database (RDS PostgreSQL 16)
docs.text:
Console: RDS → Create database → PostgreSQL 16 → Templates: Free tier/Dev-Test. Then:

  • identifier ea-hub-db, master user eahubadmin, an auto-generated or strong password
  • db.t4g.small, 20 GB gp3, the private subnets, security group ea-hub-data, Public access: No
  • Initial database name: eahub

The RDS master user is not a superuser. EA-Hub detects this and runs in owner mode: the app connects as eahubadmin, the owner of all tables. RDS enforces TLS, so set DB_SSLMODE=require.

docs.title: 6. File storage (EFS with an access point)
docs.text:
FS=$(aws efs create-file-system --encrypted --tags Key=Name,Value=ea-hub-uploads --query FileSystemId --output text)
for S in ${PRIV_SUBNETS//,/ }; do aws efs create-mount-target --file-system-id $FS --subnet-id $S --security-groups <ea-hub-data-sg-id>; done
AP=$(aws efs create-access-point --file-system-id $FS \
  --posix-user Uid=1000,Gid=0 \
  --root-directory 'Path=/ea-hub,CreationInfo={OwnerUid=1000,OwnerGid=0,Permissions=775}' \
  --query AccessPointId --output text)

The access point makes every file belong to uid 1000, the user the container runs as.

docs.title: 7. Secrets (Secrets Manager)
docs.text:
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name ea-hub/db-password    --secret-string '<RDS master password>'
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name ea-hub/enc-key        --secret-string "$(openssl rand -hex 32)"   # never change it later
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name ea-hub/cron-secret    --secret-string "$(openssl rand -hex 24)"
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name ea-hub/admin-password --secret-string '<first admin password, 10+ chars>'

The task execution role (ecsTaskExecutionRole) needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue on ea-hub/*, plus the standard AmazonECSTaskExecutionRolePolicy.

docs.title: 8. Load balancer and certificate
docs.text:
1. ACM → Request certificate for hub.example.com (DNS validation), then wait until it shows Issued.
  2. EC2 → Target groups → Create: type IP, protocol HTTP, port 3000, VPC; health check path /healthz, success code 200.
  3. EC2 → Load balancers → Create ALB: internet-facing, the public subnets, security group ea-hub-alb. Add a listener on HTTPS 443 with the ACM certificate that forwards to the target group, and a listener on HTTP 80 that redirects to HTTPS.
  4. Raise the idle timeout to 300 seconds (ALB → Attributes). Live chat uses long-lived connections.
  5. DNS: point hub.example.com to the ALB, with a Route 53 alias or a CNAME.

docs.title: 9. Task definition
docs.text:
Save as ea-hub-task.json, replacing <…>:

{
  "family": "ea-hub",
  "requiresCompatibilities": ["FARGATE"],
  "networkMode": "awsvpc",
  "cpu": "1024",
  "memory": "2048",
  "runtimePlatform": { "cpuArchitecture": "X86_64", "operatingSystemFamily": "LINUX" },
  "executionRoleArn": "arn:aws:iam::<account>:role/ecsTaskExecutionRole",
  "containerDefinitions": [
    {
      "name": "ea-hub",
      "image": "<IMAGE>",
      "essential": true,
      "portMappings": [{ "containerPort": 3000, "protocol": "tcp" }],
      "environment": [
        { "name": "APP_URL", "value": "https://hub.example.com" },
        { "name": "DB_HOST", "value": "<rds-endpoint>.rds.amazonaws.com" },
        { "name": "DB_NAME", "value": "eahub" },
        { "name": "DB_SSLMODE", "value": "require" },
        { "name": "APP_DB_USER", "value": "eahubadmin" },
        { "name": "MIGRATE_ON_START", "value": "true" },
        { "name": "ADMIN_EMAIL", "value": "admin@yourcompany.com" },
        { "name": "TRUST_PROXY_HOPS", "value": "1" }
      ],
      "secrets": [
        { "name": "APP_DB_PASSWORD", "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:ea-hub/db-password" },
        { "name": "APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY", "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:ea-hub/enc-key" },
        { "name": "CRON_SECRET", "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:ea-hub/cron-secret" },
        { "name": "ADMIN_PASSWORD", "valueFrom": "arn:aws:secretsmanager:<region>:<account>:secret:ea-hub/admin-password" }
      ],
      "mountPoints": [{ "sourceVolume": "uploads", "containerPath": "/data/storage" }],
      "healthCheck": {
        "command": ["CMD", "node", "-e", "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/healthz').then(r=>process.exit(r.ok?0:1),()=>process.exit(1))"],
        "interval": 30, "timeout": 5, "retries": 3, "startPeriod": 120
      },
      "logConfiguration": {
        "logDriver": "awslogs",
        "options": { "awslogs-group": "/ecs/ea-hub", "awslogs-region": "<region>", "awslogs-stream-prefix": "app", "awslogs-create-group": "true" }
      }
    }
  ],
  "volumes": [
    {
      "name": "uploads",
      "efsVolumeConfiguration": {
        "fileSystemId": "<FS>",
        "transitEncryption": "ENABLED",
        "authorizationConfig": { "accessPointId": "<AP>", "iam": "DISABLED" }
      }
    }
  ]
}

aws ecs register-task-definition --cli-input-json file://ea-hub-task.json

docs.title: 10. Cluster and service
docs.text:
aws ecs create-cluster --cluster-name ea-hub
aws ecs create-service --cluster ea-hub --service-name ea-hub \
  --task-definition ea-hub --desired-count 1 --launch-type FARGATE \
  --health-check-grace-period-seconds 180 \
  --network-configuration "awsvpcConfiguration={subnets=[${PRIV_SUBNETS}],securityGroups=[<ea-hub-app-sg-id>],assignPublicIp=DISABLED}" \
  --load-balancers "targetGroupArn=<target-group-arn>,containerName=ea-hub,containerPort=3000"

Watch the first start in CloudWatch Logs → /ecs/ea-hub:

[migrate] 91 migrations applied in total
[migrate] owner mode: this database does not allow BYPASSRLS …
[migrate] admin account created
➜ Listening on: http://0.0.0.0:3000/

docs.title: 11. Scheduled jobs (EventBridge Scheduler)
docs.text:
Create an IAM role ea-hub-scheduler that EventBridge Scheduler can assume (scheduler.amazonaws.com), with ecs:RunTask on the ea-hub task definition and iam:PassRole on ecsTaskExecutionRole. Then create one schedule per job:

for JOB in "newsletter|cron(0 6 * * ? *)" "daily-cleanup|cron(30 2 * * ? *)" "semantic-index|cron(15 3 * * ? *)"; do
  NAME=${JOB%%|*}; EXPR=${JOB#*|}
  aws scheduler create-schedule --name ea-hub-$NAME --schedule-expression "$EXPR" \
    --flexible-time-window Mode=OFF \
    --target "{
      \"Arn\": \"arn:aws:ecs:$REGION:$ACCOUNT:cluster/ea-hub\",
      \"RoleArn\": \"arn:aws:iam::$ACCOUNT:role/ea-hub-scheduler\",
      \"EcsParameters\": {
        \"TaskDefinitionArn\": \"arn:aws:ecs:$REGION:$ACCOUNT:task-definition/ea-hub\",
        \"LaunchType\": \"FARGATE\",
        \"NetworkConfiguration\": {\"awsvpcConfiguration\": {\"Subnets\": [\"subnet-aaa\",\"subnet-bbb\"], \"SecurityGroups\": [\"<ea-hub-app-sg-id>\"]}}
      },
      \"Input\": \"{\\\"containerOverrides\\\":[{\\\"name\\\":\\\"ea-hub\\\",\\\"command\\\":[\\\"node\\\",\\\"selfhost/scripts/run-job.mjs\\\",\\\"$NAME\\\"],\\\"environment\\\":[{\\\"name\\\":\\\"JOB_BASE_URL\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"https://$DOMAIN\\\"},{\\\"name\\\":\\\"MIGRATE_ON_START\\\",\\\"value\\\":\\\"false\\\"}]}]}\"
    }"
done

The job tasks reuse the app's task definition and only call the app with CRON_SECRET.

docs.title: 12. Open the site and sign in
docs.text:
Open https://hub.example.com/admin:

Afterwards, change the password in My account, and remove the ADMIN_PASSWORD secret from the task definition.

docs.title: 13. Operations
docs.text: Task How Upgrade push the new image tag, register a new task definition revision, aws ecs update-service --cluster ea-hub --service ea-hub --task-definition ea-hub --force-new-deployment Logs CloudWatch Logs /ecs/ea-hub Database backups RDS automated backups (7–35 days) and snapshots File backups AWS Backup plan for the EFS file system Scale --desired-count 2..3. EFS and RDS are shared, so this is safe Remove delete the service, cluster, ALB, target group, RDS instance, EFS, schedules and secrets

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Task stops with ResourceInitializationError: unable to pull secrets The execution role lacks secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, or the private subnets have no NAT / VPC endpoints mount.nfs4: Connection timed out Port 2049 is not allowed from ea-hub-app to ea-hub-data, or there is no EFS mount target in the task's subnet Target unhealthy, task keeps restarting The first start runs migrations: keep the health-check grace period at 180 s or more no pg_hba.conf entry … no encryption Set DB_SSLMODE=require Every visitor shares one rate limit Keep TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=1 behind one ALB; use 2 if CloudFront is in front of the ALB Live chat updates arrive late Raise the ALB idle timeout (step 8.4)

docs.title: Deploying EA-Hub on Azure Container Apps
docs.text:
Container Apps runs the EA-Hub container without servers or Kubernetes to manage. You combine it with three other Azure services:

EA-Hub part Azure service Web app (HTTPS, scaling) Azure Container Apps Database Azure Database for PostgreSQL – Flexible Server (version 16) Uploaded files (/data/storage) Azure Files share, mounted into the app Daily jobs Container Apps Jobs (schedule trigger) Backups built-in PostgreSQL backups + Azure Files share snapshots

Status: these steps follow Azure's documented CLI. The container itself, owner mode for managed PostgreSQL, and MIGRATE_ON_START are tested in CI on plain PostgreSQL 16. Azure itself has not been tested end-to-end yet. If something differs in your subscription, please open an issue.

Faster: a ready-made template creates all of this in one step. See deploy/cloud. This guide explains each piece, if you prefer to build it by hand or adapt it.

docs.title: Azure resources and sizing
docs.text:
Resource Starting size Notes Container App 1 vCPU, 2 GiB, min 1 / max 3 replicas min 1 replica keeps live chat and background work responsive PostgreSQL Flexible Server Burstable B1ms (1 vCore, 2 GiB), 32 GiB storage, version 16 General Purpose D2ds_v5 for production Storage account + file share Standard LRS, 5 GiB quota Premium for heavy upload traffic Container Apps Jobs 0.25 vCPU / 0.5 GiB each 3 jobs, run once a day

Rough cost at the starting sizes: about USD 40–70 per month, depending on region and traffic.

docs.title: Tools and permissions
docs.text: Need Detail Azure subscription Contributor on a resource group (or the subscription) Azure CLI 2.60+ with the extension: az extension add --name containerapp --upgrade Providers registered az provider register -n Microsoft.App and -n Microsoft.OperationalInsights The image ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version> with a GitHub token (read:packages) if it is private, or copy it to Azure Container Registry: az acr import -n <acr> --source ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version> -u <user> -p <token> A domain (optional) to use hub.example.com instead of the generated *.azurecontainerapps.io address openssl to generate secrets

docs.title: 2. Set variables
docs.text:
RG=ea-hub-rg; LOC=westeurope
ENV=ea-hub-env; APP=ea-hub
PG=ea-hub-pg-$RANDOM; PG_ADMIN=eahubadmin; PG_PASS=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
SA=eahubfiles$RANDOM; SHARE=uploads
IMAGE=ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<version>
ENC_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 32); CRON_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@yourcompany.com; ADMIN_PASSWORD='choose-a-long-password'
az group create -n $RG -l $LOC

Save PG_PASS, ENC_KEY and CRON_SECRET in your password manager now. ENC_KEY must never change once the app has started.

docs.title: 3. Create the database
docs.text:
az postgres flexible-server create -g $RG -n $PG -l $LOC \
  --version 16 --tier Burstable --sku-name Standard_B1ms --storage-size 32 \
  --admin-user $PG_ADMIN --admin-password "$PG_PASS" \
  --public-access 0.0.0.0          # allows Azure services only; use --vnet for private networking
az postgres flexible-server db create -g $RG -s $PG -d eahub

The admin account of a managed server is not a superuser. EA-Hub detects this and runs in owner mode, where the app connects with the admin account that owns the tables, so nothing else is needed.

docs.title: 4. Create the file share for uploads
docs.text:
az storage account create -g $RG -n $SA -l $LOC --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2
az storage share-rm create -g $RG --storage-account $SA -n $SHARE --quota 5
SA_KEY=$(az storage account keys list -g $RG -n $SA --query [0].value -o tsv)

docs.title: 5. Create the Container Apps environment and attach the share
docs.text:
az containerapp env create -g $RG -n $ENV -l $LOC
az containerapp env storage set -g $RG -n $ENV --storage-name uploads \
  --azure-file-account-name $SA --azure-file-account-key "$SA_KEY" \
  --azure-file-share-name $SHARE --access-mode ReadWrite

docs.title: 6. Create the app
docs.text:
The volume mount requires a YAML definition. Create ea-hub-app.yaml; the ${…} values are filled in by envsubst below:

properties:
  configuration:
    ingress: { external: true, targetPort: 3000, transport: auto, allowInsecure: false }
    secrets:
      - { name: db-password, value: "${PG_PASS}" }
      - { name: enc-key, value: "${ENC_KEY}" }
      - { name: cron-secret, value: "${CRON_SECRET}" }
      - { name: admin-password, value: "${ADMIN_PASSWORD}" }
      - { name: ghcr-token, value: "${GHCR_TOKEN}" }
    registries:
      - { server: ghcr.io, username: "${GHCR_USER}", passwordSecretRef: ghcr-token }
  template:
    containers:
      - name: ea-hub
        image: "${IMAGE}"
        resources: { cpu: 1.0, memory: 2Gi }
        env:
          - { name: APP_URL, value: "${APP_URL}" }
          - { name: DB_HOST, value: "${PG}.postgres.database.azure.com" }
          - { name: DB_NAME, value: eahub }
          - { name: DB_SSLMODE, value: require }
          - { name: APP_DB_USER, value: "${PG_ADMIN}" }
          - { name: APP_DB_PASSWORD, secretRef: db-password }
          - { name: APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, secretRef: enc-key }
          - { name: CRON_SECRET, secretRef: cron-secret }
          - { name: MIGRATE_ON_START, value: "true" }
          - { name: ADMIN_EMAIL, value: "${ADMIN_EMAIL}" }
          - { name: ADMIN_PASSWORD, secretRef: admin-password }
          - { name: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS, value: "1" }
        volumeMounts:
          - { volumeName: uploads, mountPath: /data/storage }
        probes:
          - { type: Liveness, httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 3000 }, periodSeconds: 30 }
          - { type: Readiness, httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 3000 }, periodSeconds: 10 }
          - { type: Startup, httpGet: { path: /healthz, port: 3000 }, periodSeconds: 10, failureThreshold: 30 }
    scale: { minReplicas: 1, maxReplicas: 3 }
    volumes:
      - name: uploads
        storageType: AzureFile
        storageName: uploads
        mountOptions: "uid=1000,gid=0,dir_mode=0775,file_mode=0664"

Create the app. The address isn't known yet, so a placeholder is used first:

export PG PG_ADMIN PG_PASS ENC_KEY CRON_SECRET ADMIN_EMAIL ADMIN_PASSWORD IMAGE
export GHCR_USER=<github-user> GHCR_TOKEN=<token-with-read:packages>   # drop "registries" if the image is public / in ACR
export APP_URL=https://placeholder.invalid
envsubst < ea-hub-app.yaml > /tmp/app.yaml
az containerapp create -g $RG -n $APP --environment $ENV --yaml /tmp/app.yaml

Then set the real address and update:

FQDN=$(az containerapp show -g $RG -n $APP --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv)
export APP_URL=https://$FQDN
envsubst < ea-hub-app.yaml > /tmp/app.yaml
az containerapp update -g $RG -n $APP --yaml /tmp/app.yaml
echo $APP_URL

On the first start, the app prepares the database (1–2 minutes) and creates the admin. Watch it:

az containerapp logs show -g $RG -n $APP --follow
# [migrate] 91 migrations applied in total … [migrate] owner mode: … [migrate] admin account created … Listening on: http://0.0.0.0:3000/

docs.title: 7. Scheduled jobs (replaces Vercel Cron)
docs.text:
for JOB in "newsletter|0 6 * * *" "daily-cleanup|30 2 * * *" "semantic-index|15 3 * * *"; do
  NAME=${JOB%%|*}; CRON=${JOB#*|}
  az containerapp job create -g $RG -n ea-hub-$NAME --environment $ENV \
    --trigger-type Schedule --cron-expression "$CRON" --replica-timeout 900 --replica-retry-limit 1 \
    --image $IMAGE --cpu 0.25 --memory 0.5Gi \
    --registry-server ghcr.io --registry-username $GHCR_USER --registry-password $GHCR_TOKEN \
    --secrets cron-secret=$CRON_SECRET \
    --env-vars JOB_BASE_URL=$APP_URL CRON_SECRET=secretref:cron-secret \
    --command node --args selfhost/scripts/run-job.mjs $NAME
done

Schedules are in UTC. Run one now to test it:

az containerapp job start -g $RG -n ea-hub-daily-cleanup

docs.title: 8. Your own domain (optional)
docs.text:
az containerapp hostname add -g $RG -n $APP --hostname hub.example.com
# create the DNS records it prints (CNAME to the app + TXT asuid.hub.example.com), then:
az containerapp hostname bind -g $RG -n $APP --hostname hub.example.com --environment $ENV --validation-method CNAME

Then set APP_URL=https://hub.example.com (step 6, update again) and JOB_BASE_URL on the three jobs (az containerapp job update … --set-env-vars JOB_BASE_URL=…).

docs.title: 9. Open the site and sign in
docs.text:
Open $APP_URL/admin and sign in with ADMIN_EMAIL / ADMIN_PASSWORD:

Afterwards, change the password in My account and remove the admin-password secret and the ADMIN_PASSWORD variable from the app.

docs.title: 10. Operations
docs.text: Task How Upgrade az containerapp update -g $RG -n $APP --image ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:<new>. The database is updated on start Logs az containerapp logs show -g $RG -n $APP --follow, or Log Analytics Database backups automatic, 7–35 days (az postgres flexible-server update --backup-retention 14); restore with az postgres flexible-server restore File backups Storage account → File shares → uploads → Snapshots (or Azure Backup for file shares) Scale change minReplicas / maxReplicas. Several replicas share the same file share and database Delete everything az group delete -n $RG

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Revision fails, logs show password authentication failed Wrong APP_DB_USER / password. Use the Flexible Server admin login (no @server suffix) no pg_hba.conf entry … SSL off DB_SSLMODE=require is missing connection timed out to the database Allow Azure services in the server's Networking page, or use VNet integration Upload fails with EACCES The file-share mount options must give uid 1000 write access (mountOptions in step 6) Every visitor shares one rate limit The client IP is read from X-Forwarded-For; keep TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=1, or set 2 if you put Azure Front Door in front Jobs fail with HTTP 401 The jobs' CRON_SECRET differs from the app's

docs.title: Deploying EA-Hub with Docker (one machine)
docs.text: The simplest way to run EA-Hub, on a laptop to try it out, on an office server for internal use, or on a cloud virtual machine for the internet. A setup wizard asks a few questions and starts everything with one command.

docs.title: What runs
docs.text: Service Purpose db PostgreSQL 16. Data is kept in the Docker volume db-data migrate Prepares the database and the first admin, then exits. That is normal app The EA-Hub web app. Uploads are kept in the volume storage-data caddy Front web server, with automatic free HTTPS when you use a domain name cron Daily jobs: newsletter, cleanup, search index backup Daily backup of the database and uploads into ./backups

docs.title: Hardware
docs.text: Minimum Recommended CPU 2 cores 4 cores Memory 4 GB (2 GB works for a quick try) 8 GB Disk 10 GB free 30 GB+ SSD (backups grow over time) Architecture x86-64 (amd64) arm64 works when you build the image yourself

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
Software Linux server Windows 10/11 macOS Docker Engine 24+ with Compose v2 curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com \| sh Docker Desktop (WSL 2 backend) Docker Desktop git (optional) sudo apt install git git for Windows xcode-select --install

Check:

docker version          # Server: Docker Engine 24 or newer
docker compose version  # Docker Compose version v2.x

docs.title: Network (only for internet access with HTTPS)
docs.text:
• A domain or sub-domain (e.g. hub.example.com) with a DNS A record pointing to the machine's public IP.
  • Ports 80 and 443 open to the internet: sudo ufw allow 80,443/tcp on Ubuntu, plus your cloud's firewall or security group.

docs.title: 2. Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/E20E-Tools/ea-hub-selfhost.git
cd ea-hub-selfhost

Without git: download the ZIP from the repository page (Code → Download ZIP) and extract it.

docs.title: 3. Run the setup wizard
docs.text:
./setup.sh                 # Linux / macOS

.\setup.ps1                # Windows PowerShell
# if blocked: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\setup.ps1

The wizard asks:

Question Example Notes Site address hub.example.com, 192.168.1.10, or empty With a domain it offers automatic HTTPS Admin e-mail and password admin@company.com Press Enter to generate a password; it is shown once Postgres password Enter Generated (recommended) SMTP optional Needed for "forgot password" e-mails OpenAI / Turnstile keys optional Each feature turns on only if its key is set

It writes everything to .env, including random APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, CRON_SECRET and database passwords. Then it asks "Start EA-Hub now?": answer yes.

The first start downloads or builds the image, which takes 3–10 minutes. If the published image cannot be downloaded, the wizard builds it on your machine automatically.

docs.title: Without the wizard
docs.text:
cp .env.example .env
# edit .env: APP_URL, SITE_ADDRESS, ADMIN_EMAIL, ADMIN_PASSWORD, and four random values:
#   POSTGRES_PASSWORD, APP_DB_PASSWORD, APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, CRON_SECRET   (openssl rand -hex 32)
docker compose up -d

docs.title: 4. Check that it runs
docs.text:
docker compose ps

NAME               SERVICE   STATUS
ea-hub-app-1       app       Up 2 minutes (healthy)
ea-hub-backup-1    backup    Up 2 minutes
ea-hub-caddy-1     caddy     Up 2 minutes
ea-hub-cron-1      cron      Up 2 minutes
ea-hub-db-1        db        Up 2 minutes (healthy)

migrate is not in the list because it has finished, which is expected. See what it did with docker compose logs migrate:

[migrate] 91 migrations applied in total
[migrate] admin account created
[migrate] done

Then check the health endpoint:

curl http://localhost/healthz        # {"ok":true,"database":"ok"}

docs.title: 5. Open the site and sign in
docs.text:
Open the address the wizard printed, e.g. http://localhost or https://hub.example.com, then go to /admin:

Sign in with the admin e-mail and password:

Afterwards, change the password under My account, then clear ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env. The account already exists, so the value is no longer needed.

docs.title: 6. HTTPS options
docs.text: Situation What to enter in the wizard Public domain, internet access the domain, answer yes to automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt via Caddy) Internal network, no domain the server's IP address; the site runs on HTTP inside the network Internal name with HTTPS the name, answer no; then set SITE_ADDRESS=https://hub.corp.local and APP_URL=https://hub.corp.local in .env and uncomment tls internal in deploy/compose/Caddyfile Port 80 already in use enter another HTTP port (e.g. 8080) when asked

docs.title: 7. Day-to-day operations
docs.text:
Task Command Status docker compose ps Live app log docker compose logs -f app Update to the newest version git pull && docker compose pull && docker compose up -d (if you build locally, use docker compose build instead of pull) Backup now docker compose exec backup sh /backup/backup.sh now List backups docker compose exec backup sh /backup/backup.sh list Restore docker compose stop app cron → docker compose exec backup sh /backup/backup.sh restore <name> → docker compose start app cron Change a setting edit .env (or rerun the wizard, which keeps existing secrets), then docker compose up -d Reset the admin password put the new password in ADMIN_PASSWORD, set ADMIN_RESET_PASSWORD=true, then run docker compose up -d --force-recreate migrate app; set it back to false afterwards Stop (keeps all data) docker compose down Delete everything, including data docker compose down -v

Backups are written to ./backups every day at BACKUP_HOUR_UTC (01:00 by default) and kept for BACKUP_KEEP_DAYS (14). Copy that folder and your .env off the machine regularly.

Never change APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY or POSTGRES_PASSWORD after the first start.

docs.title: Rotate secrets
docs.text:
selfhost/scripts/rotate-secrets.sh all        # or: app-db | postgres | cron | metrics

The script writes new random values to .env (the old file is kept as .env.bak-<time>), changes the database passwords in PostgreSQL, and recreates the containers that use them. Nothing is printed. After rotating metrics, copy the new METRICS_TOKEN from .env into your Prometheus scrape config. APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY is never rotated.

docs.title: 8. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Fix APP_URL is missing — run ./setup.sh There is no .env yet: run the wizard migrate exited with an error docker compose logs migrate. password authentication failed means POSTGRES_PASSWORD changed after the first start: restore it Site unreachable from other machines Open the firewall port; check that curl http://localhost/healthz works on the server itself No HTTPS certificate The DNS A record must point to this machine and ports 80/443 must be reachable; see docker compose logs caddy denied when pulling ghcr.io/… Run docker login ghcr.io, or build locally with docker compose build Links or images use the wrong address APP_URL must be exactly what users type; fix it, then docker compose up -d

More, with explanations in Arabic: docs/troubleshooting.md.

docs.title: Deploying EA-Hub on Google Cloud Run
docs.text:
Cloud Run runs the EA-Hub container with automatic HTTPS and no servers to manage. On Google Cloud:

EA-Hub part Google Cloud service Web app + HTTPS Cloud Run service Database Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 16, reached over a private IP Uploaded files (/data/storage) Cloud Storage bucket mounted as a volume Secrets Secret Manager Daily jobs Cloud Scheduler calling the app's job endpoints Image Artifact Registry Backups Cloud SQL automated backups + bucket object versioning

Status: these steps follow Google Cloud's documented gcloud commands. The container itself, owner mode for managed PostgreSQL, and MIGRATE_ON_START are tested in CI on plain PostgreSQL 16. Google Cloud itself has not been tested end-to-end yet.

Prefer Kubernetes? Use GKE with the Helm chart: deploy-kubernetes.md.

Faster: a ready-made template creates all of this in one step. See deploy/cloud. This guide explains each piece, if you prefer to build it by hand or adapt it.

docs.title: Resources and sizing
docs.text:
Resource Starting size Cloud Run service 1 vCPU, 2 GiB, min instances 1, max 3, CPU always allocated Cloud SQL db-custom-1-3840 (1 vCPU, 3.75 GB) or db-g1-small for tests, 10 GB SSD, PostgreSQL 16, private IP Cloud Storage 1 regional bucket in the same region Cloud Scheduler 3 jobs

Rough cost at these sizes: about USD 50–80 per month.

Why min 1 instance with CPU always allocated? Live chat keeps a database LISTEN connection, and background work runs after responses. Both stop when Cloud Run throttles CPU between requests.

docs.title: Tools and permissions
docs.text: Need Detail Google Cloud project with billing roles: Cloud Run Admin, Cloud SQL Admin, Storage Admin, Secret Manager Admin, Artifact Registry Admin, Cloud Scheduler Admin, Compute Network Admin, Service Account User gcloud CLI latest, gcloud auth login && gcloud config set project <PROJECT> APIs enabled gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com sqladmin.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com secretmanager.googleapis.com cloudscheduler.googleapis.com servicenetworking.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com The source or image Cloud Run pulls only from Artifact Registry (or Docker Hub), so step 3 builds the image there Domain (optional) for hub.example.com instead of the *.run.app address

docs.title: 2. Variables
docs.text:
PROJECT=$(gcloud config get-value project); REGION=europe-west1
SQL=ea-hub-sql; DB_PASS=$(openssl rand -hex 24)
BUCKET=$PROJECT-ea-hub-uploads
AR=$REGION-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT/ea-hub
SA=ea-hub-run@$PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com

docs.title: 3. Build the image into Artifact Registry
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/E20E-Tools/ea-hub-selfhost.git && cd ea-hub-selfhost
gcloud artifacts repositories create ea-hub --repository-format=docker --location=$REGION
gcloud builds submit --tag $AR/ea-hub-selfhost:1.0.0 --machine-type=e2-highcpu-8 --timeout=40m .

docs.title: 4. Private networking for Cloud SQL (once per VPC)
docs.text:
gcloud compute addresses create google-managed-services-default \
  --global --purpose=VPC_PEERING --prefix-length=16 --network=default
gcloud services vpc-peerings connect --service=servicenetworking.googleapis.com \
  --ranges=google-managed-services-default --network=default

docs.title: 5. Database (Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 16)
docs.text:
gcloud sql instances create $SQL --database-version=POSTGRES_16 --region=$REGION \
  --tier=db-custom-1-3840 --storage-size=10 --network=default --no-assign-ip \
  --backup-start-time=01:00
gcloud sql users set-password postgres --instance=$SQL --password="$DB_PASS"
gcloud sql databases create eahub --instance=$SQL
DB_IP=$(gcloud sql instances describe $SQL --format='value(ipAddresses[0].ipAddress)')

Cloud SQL's postgres user is not a real superuser. EA-Hub detects this and runs in owner mode: the app connects as postgres, the owner of all its tables.

docs.title: 6. Bucket for uploads
docs.text:
gcloud storage buckets create gs://$BUCKET --location=$REGION --uniform-bucket-level-access
gcloud storage buckets update gs://$BUCKET --versioning          # keeps deleted/overwritten files recoverable

docs.title: 7. Service account and secrets
docs.text:
gcloud iam service-accounts create ea-hub-run
gcloud storage buckets add-iam-policy-binding gs://$BUCKET --member=serviceAccount:$SA --role=roles/storage.objectUser

printf %s "$DB_PASS"                   | gcloud secrets create ea-hub-db-password --data-file=-
openssl rand -hex 32 | tr -d '\n'      | gcloud secrets create ea-hub-enc-key --data-file=-       # never change it later
openssl rand -hex 24 | tr -d '\n'      | gcloud secrets create ea-hub-cron-secret --data-file=-
printf %s 'choose-a-long-password'     | gcloud secrets create ea-hub-admin-password --data-file=-
for S in ea-hub-db-password ea-hub-enc-key ea-hub-cron-secret ea-hub-admin-password; do
  gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding $S --member=serviceAccount:$SA --role=roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor
done

docs.title: 8. Deploy the service
docs.text:
gcloud run deploy ea-hub --region=$REGION --image=$AR/ea-hub-selfhost:1.0.0 \
  --service-account=$SA --port=3000 --cpu=1 --memory=2Gi \
  --min-instances=1 --max-instances=3 --no-cpu-throttling --timeout=3600 \
  --allow-unauthenticated \
  --network=default --subnet=default --vpc-egress=private-ranges-only \
  --add-volume=name=uploads,type=cloud-storage,bucket=$BUCKET,mount-options="uid=1000;gid=0;file-mode=664;dir-mode=775" \
  --add-volume-mount=volume=uploads,mount-path=/data/storage \
  --set-env-vars=APP_URL=https://placeholder.invalid,DB_HOST=$DB_IP,DB_NAME=eahub,DB_SSLMODE=require,APP_DB_USER=postgres,MIGRATE_ON_START=true,ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@yourcompany.com,TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=1 \
  --set-secrets=APP_DB_PASSWORD=ea-hub-db-password:latest,APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY=ea-hub-enc-key:latest,CRON_SECRET=ea-hub-cron-secret:latest,ADMIN_PASSWORD=ea-hub-admin-password:latest

Now set the real address and redeploy. This only changes the environment:

URL=$(gcloud run services describe ea-hub --region=$REGION --format='value(status.url)')
gcloud run services update ea-hub --region=$REGION --update-env-vars=APP_URL=$URL
echo $URL

Watch the first start in Cloud Run → ea-hub → Logs, or:

gcloud beta run services logs tail ea-hub --region=$REGION
# [migrate] 91 migrations applied in total … owner mode … admin account created … Listening on: http://0.0.0.0:3000/

docs.title: 9. Scheduled jobs (Cloud Scheduler)
docs.text:
Cloud Scheduler calls the app's job endpoints with the cron secret, just as Vercel Cron did:

CRON=$(gcloud secrets versions access latest --secret=ea-hub-cron-secret)
for JOB in "newsletter|0 6 * * *" "daily-cleanup|30 2 * * *" "semantic-index|15 3 * * *"; do
  NAME=${JOB%%|*}; SCHED=${JOB#*|}
  gcloud scheduler jobs create http ea-hub-$NAME --location=$REGION --schedule="$SCHED" --time-zone=Etc/UTC \
    --uri="$URL/api/public/jobs/$NAME" --http-method=GET \
    --headers="Authorization=Bearer $CRON" --attempt-deadline=900s
done
gcloud scheduler jobs run ea-hub-daily-cleanup --location=$REGION   # test one now

If you rotate the cron secret, update these jobs too.

docs.title: 10. Your own domain (optional)
docs.text:
Use Cloud Run → Manage custom domains (domain mappings, where available), or put a global external Application Load Balancer with a serverless NEG and a Google-managed certificate in front. Afterwards:

  • gcloud run services update ea-hub --region=$REGION --update-env-vars=APP_URL=https://hub.example.com
  • update the three Scheduler URIs
  • behind a load balancer, set TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=2 (the load balancer adds its own address to X-Forwarded-For)

docs.title: 11. Open the site and sign in
docs.text:
Open $URL/admin:

Afterwards, change the password in My account, then remove ADMIN_PASSWORD: gcloud run services update ea-hub --region=$REGION --remove-secrets=ADMIN_PASSWORD.

docs.title: 12. Operations
docs.text: Task How Upgrade build a new tag (step 3), then gcloud run deploy ea-hub --region=$REGION --image=$AR/ea-hub-selfhost:<new>. The database is updated on start Logs Cloud Run → Logs, or Logs Explorer Database backups daily automatic backups plus point-in-time recovery: gcloud sql instances patch $SQL --enable-point-in-time-recovery File backups object versioning (step 6); optionally a second bucket with Storage Transfer Scale --max-instances. Instances share the bucket and the database Remove delete the service, Scheduler jobs, Cloud SQL instance, bucket, secrets and the Artifact Registry repository

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix connect ETIMEDOUT to the database Direct VPC egress is missing (--network/--subnet/--vpc-egress), or private services access (step 4) was not set up no pg_hba.conf entry … no encryption Set DB_SSLMODE=require Uploads fail with EACCES The bucket mount options must give uid 1000 write access (step 8), and the service account needs roles/storage.objectUser Container fails to start within the timeout The first start runs migrations; Cloud Run waits up to 4 minutes by default. Check the logs for the [migrate] lines Live chat updates arrive late Keep --no-cpu-throttling and --min-instances=1 Scheduler jobs get HTTP 401 The Authorization: Bearer … header must match the current ea-hub-cron-secret

docs.title: Deploying EA-Hub on local Kubernetes (Docker Desktop, kind, minikube, k3s)
docs.text: Use this guide to run the real Helm chart on your own computer, to learn it, test changes, or demo EA-Hub, without a cloud account. For production, follow deploy-kubernetes.md. The steps are the same, with a real domain and HTTPS.

docs.title: Hardware (your computer)
docs.text: Minimum Recommended CPU 4 cores 6+ cores Memory 8 GB (allow 4 GB for Docker / the cluster) 16 GB (6 GB for the cluster) Free disk 20 GB 40 GB

docs.title: Software
docs.text:
Tool Version Install Docker Docker Desktop 4.x, or Docker Engine 24+ docker.com One local cluster see the table below kubectl 1.27+ included in Docker Desktop; otherwise kubernetes.io Helm 3.8+ or 4.x winget install Helm.Helm · brew install helm · helm.sh git any Local cluster Good for Install Docker Desktop Kubernetes Windows/macOS users who already have Docker Desktop Docker Desktop → Settings → Kubernetes → Enable Kubernetes kind fastest to create and throw away; what our CI uses winget install Kubernetes.kind · brew install kind minikube many add-ons (ingress, dashboard) winget install Kubernetes.minikube · brew install minikube k3s a Linux machine or VM, closest to a small production server curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io \| sh -

All four include a default StorageClass, which EA-Hub needs for its volumes.

docs.title: 2. Create or start the cluster
docs.text:
# kind
kind create cluster --name ea-hub

# minikube
minikube start --memory 6g --cpus 4

# Docker Desktop: enable Kubernetes in Settings, then select its context
kubectl config use-context docker-desktop

# k3s: already running after installation
mkdir -p ~/.kube && sudo cp /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml ~/.kube/config && sudo chown $USER ~/.kube/config

Check:

kubectl get nodes           # STATUS Ready
kubectl get storageclass    # one is marked (default)

docs.title: 3. Get the code and build the image
docs.text:
Building locally avoids needing access to the published image.

git clone https://github.com/E20E-Tools/ea-hub-selfhost.git
cd ea-hub-selfhost
docker build --build-arg WITH_LOCAL_MODEL=0 -t ea-hub-selfhost:local .

WITH_LOCAL_MODEL=0 makes the image ~120 MB smaller by leaving out the local search model. The build takes 5–10 minutes the first time.

Make the image visible to the cluster:

Cluster Command kind kind load docker-image ea-hub-selfhost:local --name ea-hub minikube minikube image load ea-hub-selfhost:local Docker Desktop nothing to do, the cluster uses Docker's images k3s docker save ea-hub-selfhost:local \| sudo k3s ctr images import -

docs.title: 4. Install with Helm
docs.text:
helm upgrade --install ea-hub deploy/helm/ea-hub \
  --namespace ea-hub --create-namespace \
  --set image.repository=ea-hub-selfhost \
  --set image.tag=local \
  --set image.pullPolicy=Never \
  --set appUrl=http://localhost:8080 \
  --set admin.email=admin@example.com \
  --set admin.password='choose-a-long-password' \
  --set backup.storage.size=2Gi --set storage.size=1Gi --set postgres.storage.size=2Gi

Wait until it is ready. The first start prepares the database, which takes 1–3 minutes:

kubectl -n ea-hub rollout status deploy/ea-hub --timeout=10m
kubectl -n ea-hub get pods

NAME                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
ea-hub-6d8f9c7b8d-q4z2n   1/1     Running   0          2m
ea-hub-postgres-0         1/1     Running   0          2m

docs.title: 5. Open the site
docs.text:
kubectl -n ea-hub port-forward svc/ea-hub 8080:80

Keep that command running, then open http://localhost:8080/admin and sign in with the e-mail and password from step 4.

The address in appUrl must match the one you open (http://localhost:8080), otherwise links and uploaded images point elsewhere.

docs.title: Optional: use an Ingress instead of port-forward
docs.text:
• minikube: run minikube addons enable ingress, then add --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.host=ea-hub.local --set appUrl=http://ea-hub.local. Point ea-hub.local to minikube ip in your hosts file.
  • k3s: Traefik is built in. Use the same flags, with ingress.className=traefik, and point the name to the machine's IP.

docs.title: 6. Try the scheduled jobs and the backup
docs.text:
kubectl -n ea-hub create job --from=cronjob/ea-hub-daily-cleanup cleanup-now
kubectl -n ea-hub create job --from=cronjob/ea-hub-backup backup-now
kubectl -n ea-hub wait --for=condition=complete job/cleanup-now job/backup-now --timeout=5m
kubectl -n ea-hub logs job/backup-now

docs.title: 7. Change, upgrade, remove
docs.text:
# after rebuilding the image with a new tag (e.g. local2) and loading it again:
helm upgrade ea-hub deploy/helm/ea-hub -n ea-hub --reset-then-reuse-values --set image.tag=local2

# remove everything, including the data
helm uninstall ea-hub -n ea-hub
kubectl delete namespace ea-hub

# delete the cluster itself
kind delete cluster --name ea-hub     # or: minikube delete

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Pod Pending The cluster lacks memory: give Docker Desktop / minikube more (Settings → Resources) ErrImageNeverPull The image was not loaded into the cluster (step 3), or the tag differs Init:0/1 for a long time kubectl -n ea-hub logs deploy/ea-hub -c migrate shows the progress of the database setup Port 8080 busy Use another local port: port-forward svc/ea-hub 9090:80, and appUrl=http://localhost:9090

docs.title: Deploying EA-Hub on Kubernetes — a step-by-step guide
docs.text:
This guide is for someone new to EA-Hub who wants to run it on their own Kubernetes cluster, using either the Helm chart (recommended) or the plain YAML file (no Helm). It starts with what you need to have, then walks through every step until you are signed in to the admin console.

Other platforms (Docker, local Kubernetes, OpenShift, Rancher, Azure, AWS, Google Cloud): see the guide index.

Contents

  1. What gets deployed
  2. Requirements
  3. Step 1 — Check your tools and cluster
  4. Step 2 — Get the code
  5. Step 3 — Make the container image available
  6. Step 4 — Domain name and HTTPS (optional)
  7. Path A — Install with Helm
  8. Path B — Install with the plain YAML file
  9. Step 8 — Open the site and sign in
  10. Day-2 operations: upgrade, backup, restore, uninstall
  11. Troubleshooting
  12. Reference: all settings

docs.title: 1. What gets deployed
docs.text:
Resource Purpose Deployment ea-hub The web application (Node.js, port 3000). An init container prepares the database (schema, roles, first admin) every time a pod starts. Doing that more than once is safe. Service ea-hub Internal address of the app on port 80. Ingress ea-hub (optional) Makes the site reachable from outside under your domain, with HTTPS if you want it. StatefulSet ea-hub-postgres PostgreSQL 16 with its own persistent volume. It can be replaced by an external database. Secret ea-hub Passwords and keys. Helm generates them for you and keeps them on upgrades. PVC ea-hub-storage Uploaded files (logos, product images, attachments). PVC ea-hub-backups Daily backups. CronJobs newsletter (06:00 UTC), daily-cleanup (02:30), semantic-index (03:15), backup (01:00).

EA-Hub needs no external services to run: no Supabase, no Vercel, no cloud database. Everything lives in your cluster.

docs.title: 2.1 Hardware (cluster capacity)
docs.text:
These are the totals the chart asks for across the cluster. A single node is fine.

Minimum Recommended CPU 2 vCPU 4 vCPU Memory 4 GB RAM 8 GB RAM Disk for volumes 35 GB (5 uploads + 10 database + 20 backups) 60 GB or more, on SSD Disk for images ~3 GB free on each node (the app image is ~1 GB) CPU architecture amd64 (x86-64) arm64 is published for tagged releases

What each part requests and is allowed to use (all can be changed in values.yaml):

Container CPU request Memory request → limit app 100m 384 Mi → 1.5 Gi PostgreSQL 100m 256 Mi → 1 Gi migrate (init, short-lived) 50m 128 Mi → 512 Mi each CronJob (short-lived) 10m 64 Mi → 256 Mi

docs.title: 2.2 Software
docs.text:
Software Version Needed for How to check Kubernetes 1.27 or newer (CronJob timeZone) everything kubectl version kubectl matching your cluster ±1 minor everything kubectl version --client Helm 3.8+ or 4.x Path A only helm version git any downloading the code git --version A default StorageClass dynamic provisioning, ReadWriteOnce the volumes kubectl get storageclass (one marked (default)) An Ingress controller ingress-nginx, Traefik… reaching the site by domain (optional) kubectl get ingressclass cert-manager 1.x automatic HTTPS certificates (optional) kubectl get pods -n cert-manager Docker 24+ only if you build the image yourself docker version openssl any only for Path B (generating secrets) openssl version

No cluster yet? For a single machine (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 with the hardware above), k3s gives you everything in the table (Kubernetes, a default StorageClass and the Traefik ingress controller) with one command:

curl -sfL https://get.k3s.io | sh -
mkdir -p ~/.kube && sudo cp /etc/rancher/k3s/k3s.yaml ~/.kube/config && sudo chown $USER ~/.kube/config
kubectl get nodes        # STATUS should be Ready

Managed clusters (AKS, EKS, GKE, DigitalOcean, OpenShift…) work too.

docs.title: 2.3 Access and accounts
docs.text:
What Why Required? Access to the app image The repository is private, so its image on ghcr.io is private too. You need a GitHub account with access to E20E-Tools/ea-hub-selfhost and a personal access token with read:packages, or you build the image yourself (Step 3). yes An e-mail address for the first admin It is the sign-in name of the first administrator. yes A domain name (e.g. hub.example.com) with access to its DNS To reach the site by name with HTTPS. Without it you can still use port-forwarding or a NodePort. optional SMTP account (host, port, user, password) "Forgot password" e-mails, notifications, newsletter. optional OpenAI API key Search by meaning. optional Cloudflare Turnstile keys Bot protection on public forms. optional

Every optional feature turns itself on only when its key is set, and stays quietly off otherwise.

docs.title: 2.4 Network
docs.text:
• Users reach the site over HTTP 80 / HTTPS 443 on the ingress controller.
  • For automatic HTTPS (Let's Encrypt), ports 80 and 443 must be reachable from the internet and the DNS name must point to the ingress controller.
  • Outbound internet from the cluster is only needed for optional features (SMTP, OpenAI, certificates) and to pull images.

docs.title: Step 1 — Check your tools and cluster
docs.text:
Run these four commands. Each should print something like the example output.

kubectl version            # Server Version: v1.27 or newer
helm version               # v3.8+ or v4.x   (Path A only)
kubectl get nodes          # every node shows STATUS = Ready
kubectl get storageclass   # one line ends with "(default)"

Example of a healthy cluster:

$ kubectl get nodes
NAME      STATUS   ROLES                  AGE   VERSION
server1   Ready    control-plane,master   3d    v1.31.4+k3s1

$ kubectl get storageclass
NAME                   PROVISIONER             RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE
local-path (default)   rancher.io/local-path   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer

No (default) StorageClass? Either mark one as default (kubectl patch storageclass <name> -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class":"true"}}}') or set storage.storageClass, postgres.storage.storageClass and backup.storage.storageClass in your values.

docs.title: Step 2 — Get the code
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/E20E-Tools/ea-hub-selfhost.git
cd ea-hub-selfhost

The two folders you need:

deploy/helm/ea-hub/        ← the Helm chart (Path A)
deploy/kubernetes/         ← the plain YAML files (Path B)

docs.title: Step 3 — Make the container image available
docs.text: Pick one option.

docs.title: Option 1 — Use the published image (simplest)
docs.text:
Images are published for each release tag, e.g. ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost:1.0.0, for both amd64 and arm64. They are public, so nothing needs to be set up and you can go to Step 4.

Quickest install, no clone at all. The chart is published as well, so this one command installs everything:

helm install ea-hub oci://ghcr.io/e20e-tools/charts/ea-hub -n ea-hub --create-namespace >   --set appUrl=https://hub.example.com --set ingress.enabled=true --set ingress.host=hub.example.com >   --set admin.email=you@example.com

The classic repository works too: helm repo add ea-hub https://e20e-tools.github.io/ea-hub-selfhost. The chart is also listed on Artifact Hub.

If your organisation mirrors the image into a private registry, create a pull secret so Kubernetes can download it:

kubectl create namespace ea-hub
kubectl -n ea-hub create secret docker-registry ghcr-pull \
  --docker-server=ghcr.io \
  --docker-username=<your-github-user> \
  --docker-password=<token-with-read:packages>

You will reference ghcr-pull and the tag in Path A or B.

docs.title: Option 2 — Build the image and push it to your own registry
docs.text:
docker build -t registry.example.com/ea-hub-selfhost:1.0.0 .
docker push registry.example.com/ea-hub-selfhost:1.0.0

Add --build-arg WITH_LOCAL_MODEL=0 for a ~120 MB smaller image without the local search model.

docs.title: Option 3 — Single-node k3s without a registry
docs.text:
docker build -t ea-hub-selfhost:local .
docker save ea-hub-selfhost:local | sudo k3s ctr images import -

Then use image.repository=ea-hub-selfhost, image.tag=local and image.pullPolicy=Never.

docs.title: Step 4 — Domain name and HTTPS (optional)
docs.text:
1. Find the external address of your ingress controller: 
    kubectl get svc -A | grep -Ei 'ingress|traefik'
# look at the EXTERNAL-IP column (on k3s: the server's own IP)
  2. At your DNS provider create an A record: hub.example.com → <that IP>.
  3. For automatic certificates, install cert-manager and a Let's Encrypt issuer (once per cluster): 
    kubectl apply -f https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.16.2/cert-manager.yaml
cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    email: you@example.com
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-account
    solvers:
      - http01:
          ingress:
            ingressClassName: traefik   # or nginx
EOF

No domain? Skip this step and use port-forwarding in Step 8.

docs.title: 5A. Write your values file
docs.text:
Create my-values.yaml outside the repository (it holds secrets). Replace the values marked <…>:

# my-values.yaml
appUrl: https://hub.example.com          # exactly what people type in the browser

admin:
  email: <admin@yourcompany.com>
  password: <a-long-password-10+-chars>  # used once to create the first admin

image:
  repository: ghcr.io/e20e-tools/ea-hub-selfhost   # or your registry (Step 3)
  tag: "1.0.0"                           # an existing release tag (see the repository's Releases/Packages)
imagePullSecrets:
  - name: ghcr-pull                      # remove these two lines if the image is public/local

ingress:
  enabled: true
  className: traefik                     # nginx for ingress-nginx; "" = cluster default
  host: hub.example.com
  tls: true
  annotations:
    cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt   # remove if you have no cert-manager

# Optional — delete what you do not use
smtp:
  host: smtp.example.com
  port: 587
  user: mailer@example.com
  password: <smtp-password>
  from: "EA-Hub <mailer@example.com>"
features:
  openaiApiKey: ""
  turnstileSiteKey: ""
  turnstileSecretKey: ""

You do not need to invent database passwords or encryption keys: the chart generates them on the first install and keeps them on every upgrade.

Shortcut: ./setup.sh --helm (Linux/macOS) or .\setup.ps1 -Helm (Windows) asks you these questions and writes ea-hub-values.yaml for you.

Check the file before installing. The chart validates it against values.schema.json, so mistakes such as a malformed URL or a short password are reported here:

helm lint deploy/helm/ea-hub -f my-values.yaml
helm template ea-hub deploy/helm/ea-hub -n ea-hub -f my-values.yaml > /dev/null && echo OK

docs.title: 6A. Install
docs.text:
helm upgrade --install ea-hub deploy/helm/ea-hub \
  --namespace ea-hub --create-namespace \
  -f my-values.yaml

Helm prints the next steps (the chart's NOTES.txt):

Release "ea-hub" does not exist. Installing it now.
NAME: ea-hub
NAMESPACE: ea-hub
STATUS: deployed
REVISION: 1
NOTES:
EA-Hub is being installed in namespace "ea-hub".
…
1) Wait until it is ready / … (first start runs the database setup, 1–3 minutes):
   kubectl -n ea-hub rollout status deploy/ea-hub --timeout=10m

2) Open the site / …:
   https://hub.example.com
   (DNS for hub.example.com must point to your ingress controller.)

3) Sign in / …:  https://hub.example.com/admin
   e-mail: admin@yourcompany.com  (password: the one you set in admin.password)
…

docs.title: 7A. Wait until it is ready
docs.text:
kubectl -n ea-hub rollout status deploy/ea-hub --timeout=10m
kubectl -n ea-hub get pods

Expected:

deployment "ea-hub" successfully rolled out

NAME                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
ea-hub-7c9d6f8b5d-x2klm   1/1     Running   0          2m
ea-hub-postgres-0         1/1     Running   0          2m

While the pod shows Init:0/1, the database is being prepared. Follow it with:

kubectl -n ea-hub logs deploy/ea-hub -c migrate -f

[migrate] waiting for database on ea-hub-postgres …
[migrate] bootstrap (roles, auth, storage) …
[migrate] upstream migrations …
[migrate] 91 migrations applied in total
[migrate] post-migrate (buckets, realtime) …
[migrate] app role eahub_app ready
[migrate] admin account created
[migrate] done

Continue with Step 8.

docs.title: Path B — Install with the plain YAML file
docs.text: deploy/kubernetes/ea-hub.yaml is generated from the Helm chart. It contains no secrets: you create them yourself.

docs.title: 5B. Namespace and Secret
docs.text:
kubectl apply -f deploy/kubernetes/namespace.yaml
cp deploy/kubernetes/secret.example.yaml ~/ea-hub-secret.yaml    # keep it OUTSIDE the repository

Generate one random value for each CHANGE_ME:

openssl rand -hex 32     # run once per value

Edit ~/ea-hub-secret.yaml:

stringData:
  postgres-password: 3f1c…           # random
  app-db-password: 9ab4…             # random
  app-encryption-key: 6d02…          # random, at least 32 characters — NEVER change it later
  cron-secret: 51e7…                 # random
  admin-password: <your admin password, 10+ characters>

Then apply it:

kubectl apply -f ~/ea-hub-secret.yaml

docs.title: 6B. Put your address, admin e-mail and image into the YAML
docs.text:
